name: set_state_observer
doc:
Set a state observer (UniFFI export).

DEPRECATED: callback-based observer. Use `state_stream()` —
the callback observer pins the foreign object in UniFFI's
static handleMap and produces a cross-language retain cycle
(Android GC + iOS ARC).

name: create
doc:
Create a new Spot DCA Place Order interactor.

Each action method (`fetch_strategy_config`, `fetch_account_available`,
`fetch_preview`, `validate`, `submit`) takes its own `inst_id` /
`params` argument; the constructor itself owns no per-instrument
state. Per `interactor.md` § "Constructor", `create()` parameters
are dependencies / initial state, never unused FFI ballast.

name: calculate_est_periods
doc:
Calculate estimated number of recurring periods.
Returns `floor(balance / amount)`, or `None` if amount < min_amount.

name: remove_state_observer
doc:
Remove the state observer (UniFFI export).

DEPRECATED: callback-based observation. Use `state_stream()` —
it needs no removal call. Until migrated, every
`set_state_observer` MUST be paired with this (or `release()`)
at host lifecycle end, or the UniFFI handleMap pins the
observer and its host forever.

name: SpotGridBotInfo

fields.name: algo_ord_type
fields.doc:
Algo order type (server field `algoOrdType`). The legacy `getOrderType()`
is `ordType.ifEmpty { algoOrdType }` (StrategyDetailsResponse.kt:404-406):
some bots send the strategy type ("grid") ONLY under `algoOrdType` with an
empty top-level `ordType`. The Spot Grid Parameter tab's trailing-up/down
section gates on `getOrderType() == "grid"`, so the native composer must
apply the same fallback — reading `ord_type` alone wrongly hid the trailing
rows whenever the wire left `ordType` blank. Additive field; defaults to "".

fields.name: cancel_type
fields.doc:
Why the bot stopped (server field `cancelType`). The detail status label is resolved from
THIS, not from `state`: legacy `StrategyConvert.getGridCancelType` maps it to one of 14
reasons ("Stopped manually", take-profit, stop-loss, liquidation, ADL, delisting, ...) and
falls back to the generic "ended" string. Rendering `state` instead collapses every reason
to a bare "Stopped". Top-level plain-serde field, same as the Spot DCA record
(`dca/spot_dca/detail.rs:142-145`). Additive; defaults to "".

fields.name: c_time
fields.doc: Creation timestamp (ms)

fields.name: u_time
fields.doc: Update timestamp (ms)

fields.name: p_time
fields.doc:
Stop / pause timestamp (server field `pTime`). Shown as the "stopped
time" row in the About section for history (stopped) bots.

fields.name: rule_type
fields.doc:
Instrument rule type (server field `ruleType`). Consumed by the title
formatter (`getCoinTitleTacticsItem`) to decide raw-instId vs
display-id rendering.

fields.name: display_id
fields.doc:
Instrument display id (server field `displayId`). Title formatter
fallback when the instrument lookup yields no display id.

fields.name: stgy_name
fields.doc:
User-set strategy name (wire `bot.common.stgyName`). The header title
PREFERS this over the coin-pair label when non-empty. Nested under
`bot.common` (sibling of `autoEarn` / `autoStaking`), so serde cannot
bind it onto this flat struct — it is `#[serde(skip)]` and lifted
post-parse by `extract_stgy_name` on both the HTTP and WS paths. `""`
when absent (forward-compatible).

fields.name: is_pinned
fields.doc:
Server-persisted `bot.common.isPinned`, lifted from the nested common
block so Rust owns Pin/Unpin identity and native never inspects raw JSON.

fields.name: cur_base_fund_ratio
fields.doc:
Base-fund ratio of total holdings (wire: bot.spotGrid.curBaseFundRatio);
drives the Current-Holding donut split. The wire field is nested under
`bot.spotGrid`, not top-level, so serde cannot bind it on this flat
struct — it is populated post-parse by `extract_cur_base_fund_ratio`
on both the HTTP and WS paths. `#[serde(default)]` keeps it forward-
compatible (empty string when the nested block is absent).

fields.name: tpsl_trigger_param
fields.doc:
Structured TP/SL trigger params (wire: top-level `tpslTriggerParam`).
Drives the TP/SL display section. `None` when no TP/SL is configured.

fields.name: sign_params

fields.name: trailing_up_config

the wire block is absent.

fields.name: trailing_down_config

when the wire block is absent.

fields.name: voucher_info

the wire object is absent OR an empty `{}` (mirrors legacy

fields.name: effective_edit_parameters_details

Effective edit-parameter details (wire: top-level
`effectiveEditParametersDetails`). `None` when the wire block is absent.

fields.name: compliance_pause_display_type
fields.doc:
Compliance pause display type (wire `bot.compliancePauseDisplayType` —
nested directly under `bot`, sibling of `bot.common` / `bot.spotGrid`).

fields.name: reserve_funds
fields.doc: Whether reserve-funds is enabled for this bot (wire `reserveFunds`).

fields.name: trailing_down_fund

fields.name: auto_earn_status
fields.doc: Auto-earn status (wire `bot.common.autoEarn.status`).

fields.name: auto_staking_status
fields.doc: Auto-staking status (wire `bot.common.autoStaking.status`).

fields.name: auto_staking_total_profit

fields.name: min_follow_invest_amount
fields.doc:
Lead-trader follower minimum investment (wire `bot.common.minFollowInvestAmount`).
Nested under `bot.common` (sibling of `stgyName` / `autoEarn` / `autoStaking`),
so serde cannot bind it onto this flat struct — it is `#[serde(skip)]` and
lifted post-parse by `extract_min_follow_invest_amount` on both the HTTP and

Available overview ccys for the profit-display toggle, in BE order,
non-blank + de-duplicated (mirrors `SpotGridProfitDisplayUtil.availableCcys`).

The overview ccy the field-grid display fields (`total_pnl_display`,

fields.name: last_price_display

fields.doc:
Invested amount value (`fmtBotValueBySymbol(investUnit, investSz,
RoundingMode.UP)`): investUnit coin sizeDig, round UP, AUTO sign, no color.

coinSizeDig) of `newInstId`, round DOWN(>0)/UP(<=0), EXCEPT_ZERO sign,

fields.name: grid_profit_history_display

not `newInstId` — `TacticListDataMapper.kt:3426`). Differs from

Daily arbitrage count (`simpleEmptyConvert(info.avgDailyArbitrageNum)`):
locale integer (native ICU grouping), no sign/color; empty → `Placeholder`.

fields.name: arbitrage_num_display
fields.doc: Total arbitrage count (`simpleEmptyConvert(info.arbitrageNum)`).

fields.name: start_price_display
fields.doc:
Grid start price (`getProcessedPrice(instType, instId, runPx,
RoundingMode.UP)`): charge-currency price digit, round UP, drop trailing
zeros, no sign/color. Blank → `Placeholder`.

fields.name: grid_num_display

Grids quantity (`simpleEmptyConvert(info.gridNum)`): locale integer,
no sign/color; empty → `Placeholder`.

fields.name: share_amount_display
fields.doc:
Share amount (COPY_TYPE_SHARE_PROFIT row): `getBotPnl(instId, instType,
floatProfitValue, isShowSymbol=false)` where `floatProfitValue =
totalPnl > 0 ? totalPnl * profitSharingRatio : "0"`. max(profit, coin)
precision, DOWN(>0)/UP(<=0), AUTO sign (no "+"), no color.

fields.doc:
Single-grid order amount (`getBotAmount(instType, instId, singleAmt,
ctVal = "")`, migration #76 amount/price pass): spot path
CoinTradeConvertor(symbol, baseDig).toTargetFormatted(singleAmt).down()
.group().changeUnique().toSafeString(). baseDig =
`get_amount_digit(inst_family)` (fallback `DEFAULT_COIN_DIGIT` = 8); the
magnitude-dependent `changeUnique()` override is applied to the RAW value
(< 1000 → baseDig; >= 1_000_000 → 0; else min(baseDig, 4)). DOWN rounding,
drop trailing zeros, AUTO sign, no color. **Shared by the PARAMETER tab AND
the PENDING tab** — both render the same `info.singleAmt`. The amount-unit
suffix (`getBotAmountUnit`) stays in Kotlin (ccy-unit phase). Computed in
`apply_parameter_displays` on both parse paths.

fields.name: est_profit_margin_min_display
fields.doc:
Est-profit-margin range bounds (`fmtBotPnlPercent(perMinProfitRate)` /
`fmtBotPnlPercent(perMaxProfitRate)`, migration #86 percent pass): ×100,
2dp, PER-SIGN rounding (DOWN if ≥0, UP if <0), clamp `[0.00001, 0.0001)`
→ "0.0001", AUTO sign, no color. Pre-scaled (`pre_scaled = true`) — Rust
rounds; native scales ×1. The `min "-" max` join stays in Kotlin. Computed
in `apply_parameter_displays` on both parse paths.

fields.name: est_profit_margin_max_display
fields.doc:
Upper bound of the est-profit-margin range — see
[`est_profit_margin_min_display`].

fields.name: proportion_display

Proportion/moistening % (COPY_TYPE_SHARE_PROFIT row,
`OKTNumberF.formatPercent(profitSharingRatio, precision = 0)`, migration
#86): ×100, precision 0, UP rounding, AUTO sign, no color. Pre-scaled

isShowSymbol=true, minDigit=2)`): max(profit, coin) precision, DOWN(>0)/
UP(<=0), EXCEPT_ZERO sign ("+" for >0), MIN 2 decimals (legacy

instId, simpleEarn.activeRegionLow, RoundingMode.DOWN)`): charge-currency
price digit, round DOWN, drop trailing zeros, no sign/color. Blank /

instId, simpleEarn.activeRegionHigh, RoundingMode.DOWN)`): same as

reformat — Path A precedence (arg-displayId → bizDisplayId → instId). Used
by the Parameter-tab header and the Overview share card. SPOT only.

trade-symbol, **no delisted fallback**. Blank when the instrument is absent.

fields.name: amount_symbol_with_fallback
fields.doc:

amount): `amount_unit`, falling back to `coinFormat(instId).amountSign
.uppercase()` when blank (delisted-pair fallback).

fields.name: history_pnl_unit
fields.doc:

(History arbitraged-grid-profit suffix): `tradeQuoteCcy` when non-blank,
else the SPOT quote symbol, else `coinFormat(instId).priceSign.uppercase()`.

fields.name: history_profit_unit
fields.doc:
History filter-bar profit unit (`sourceCcy ?? tradeQuoteCcy ??
getBotFondUnit(instType, instId, "")`): the composer-level preference chain.
`getBotFondUnit` (spot) = the trade-symbol (= [`amount_unit`]).

fields.name: auto_earn_profit_display
fields.doc:
Auto-earn profit value (`formatAutoEarn(autoEarnTotalProfit, …, minDigit=2)`
→ getPnlAndColorPair): getDigitsCount precision, FLOOR, drop trailing zeros,
tiny-clamp, ExceptZero sign, colored on the ROUNDED value. minDigit is dead
in legacy → NO pad. The unit suffix is appended in Kotlin from

fields.name: auto_stake_profit_display
fields.doc:

shape as [`auto_earn_profit_display`] (legacy reuses the same leaf path).

"earning"`) AND `canShowEarnOrStakeProfit` (always true under EARNING).

`getBotPriceUnitWithFallback(instType, instId, displayId)` — the Overview
VM's `priceUnit` arg (the "Current price (USDT)" suffix + the composer's
invest-unit fallback). Resolved in Rust by `resolve_price_unit_with_fallback`

`OKTNumberF.formatLocalized(activeOrderCount)` — the Pending-tab badge
"(count)" value (BotDetailActivity.kt:324). The `count > 0` gate stays in
Kotlin; this field carries only the localized count string. `count_display`
renders the same locale-grouped integer the legacy `formatLocalized` did.

fields.name: share_price_unit
fields.doc:
`getPriceDisplaySymbol(getSuggestedInstrument(instType, instId))` — the BARE
charge price symbol (`get_price_display_symbol(inst)`, `.orEmpty()`). Feeds
ONLY the price-range title's `{ccy}` placeholder (the legacy `unit` arg),

`getProfitSymbol(instId, instType, sourceCcy)` = `sourceCcy` when non-blank,
else `instrument.get_profit_symbol()`. The legacy `ShareData.priceUnit` field
= `sourceCcy.ifBlank(this)`, which equals this value either way, so it is

`BotConverter.getPnlUnit(instId, instType)` (no investmentCcy) — the
`ShareData.pnlUnit` field. SPOT → instrument quote symbol, else
`coinFormat(instId).priceSign.uppercase()` (same chain as `resolve_pnl_unit`

`OKTNumberF.formatLocalized(arbitrageNum)` — the `botDataValue1` arbitrage
times. `count_display` (blank → Placeholder "--"; native ICU groups).

fields.name: share_price_range_min

Price-range LOW bound — `getPriceRange`'s `convertor.toQuoteFormatted(minPx)
.round().group()` (charge-currency price digit, HALF_UP, drop trailing
zeros). `Placeholder` when min is blank.

fields.name: share_price_range_max

fields.name: share_price_range_available

Whether the price range resolved (`getPriceRange` did NOT return its `noData`
sentinel): min AND max non-blank AND the instrument/charge convertor present.
When `false`, the legacy returns `("", null)` → Kotlin sets
`botDataTitle2 = ""` and `botDataValue2 = null` (the row is hidden). When

doc:
Spot Grid / Spot DCA Bot Info — parsed from
`/priapi/v5/algo/trade/info`. Field names match the wire JSON. The
same struct is used for the SpotGrid + SpotDca variants (both share
the trade-info schema); Contract Grid has its own larger record in
`contract_grid::detail`. Despite the historical name, this Record
is also consumed by the DCA detail screen.
Every wire field is a strict `String`: one bare number or `null` fails the whole parse.
Ramp on one bot type proves nothing about a field only another type populates.
Declare per field what the wire actually sends; do not blanket-widen this struct.

doc:
Full parameter set passed to `submit`.

`#[derive(uniffi::Record)]` is required here because the `#[interactor::actions]`
proc-macro exports every action method via UniFFI, and all action parameters
must implement `uniffi::Lift`. This is a framework constraint, not a
promote-on-demand violation — the record is the interactor's FFI surface.

**Percent-field unit — DELIBERATE asymmetry with the create path, do not "fix":**
`tp_pct` / `sl_pct` / `px_steps` / `px_steps_mult` here carry an ALREADY-DIVIDED
fraction (e.g. `"0.02"` for 2%) — `submit()` forwards them to `ParametersEditsRequest`
verbatim, with NO `div_by_100`. This is the opposite convention from
`place_order::SpotDcaPlaceOrderParams`, whose same-named fields carry the raw UI
percent and get divided internally. The caller (native) already applies
`OKTNumberF.formatHundredQuot` before populating this Record on the edit path — the
same split exists in `contract_dca::edit_params::SpotDcaEditParamsInput` vs
`contract_dca::place_order`, so this is an established cross-bot-family pattern, not
a one-off bug. Harmonizing either side alone breaks the wire for whichever native
caller still relies on the current contract.

name: WithdrawActionState
doc:
Submit / liquidation-price-preview channel only — NOT the profits GET.

name: create_chrome
doc:
Shared host-chrome projection for `BotPlaceOrderActivity` /
`BotPlaceOrderChromeBinder`; mirrors `SpotGridPlaceOrderInteractor::
create_chrome` / `ContractDcaPlaceOrderInteractor::create_chrome` (see
`BotCreateChrome`'s own doc comment for the field contract).

Field sourcing:
- `pair_label`: `format_trade_title(inst_id, "SPOT")`. The hardcoded
`"SPOT"` inst type mirrors `SpotGridPlaceOrderInteractor::
create_chrome` for the same reason it applies there: Spot DCA only
ever trades SPOT instruments (the SAME assumption already baked
into this bot's OTHER formatters — see `resolve_profit_digit`'s "For
SPOT the inst family equals the inst id" and `spot_dca::detail.rs::
dca_resolve_price_digit`), and no resolved inst-type field exists
anywhere on `SpotDcaPlaceOrderState` to source anything else from.
`inst_id` itself is `active_instrument` — the pair every action
already serializes its requests against via `observe_instrument`,
not a second lookup. `CTTradeTitle::default()` while no pair has
been observed yet.
- `ticker`: `state.market_price` — on Android the self-fed
`InstTickerDataSource` value (`InstTickerCallback::on_refreshed`), on
iOS the native `set_market_price` push; both land on
`apply_live_market_price` — plus `state.last_px_tone`
(`apply_market_price_tone`, run there BEFORE the field is overwritten
— the same algorithm Contract DCA's `apply_last_px_tone` / Spot Grid's
`apply_market_price` use). Price digit via `create_order_format::
resolve_price_digit(inst_id)` — the same charge-currency
index-config lookup `spot_dca::detail.rs::dca_resolve_price_digit`
already uses for this bot's other price fields (a local
`Trade::instance()` index read, not network I/O — not a second
instrument lookup). Absent/hidden (`Placeholder` / `Neutral` /
`false`) while no positive price has arrived yet — same gate as
Contract DCA's `create_chrome`.
- `toolbar_more_visible`: `true` — the same provisional literal Spot
Grid / Contract DCA / TWAP's shared-host overflow entry use today;
no real business source has surfaced for Spot DCA either.
- `toolbar_strategy_switch_enabled`: always `false` — Spot DCA has no
strategy-selector catalog (no such field exists on
`SpotDcaPlaceOrderState`), so switching strategies from this screen
is never offered from Rust state today. A real, sourced "no", not a
stand-in for missing data.
- `leverage`: `None` — Spot DCA is a spot bot; legacy only paints the
margin-leverage badge for Smart Iceberg / TWAP on a spot-margin
instrument (`BotTradeHeader.refreshCoinPairsNormal`, read-only
oracle), a gate Spot DCA never reaches. See `BotCreateChrome::
leverage`'s own doc comment.

fields.name: pair_label
fields.doc:
Formatted pair label (e.g. `"BTC/USDT"`), NOT the raw `inst_id`.

First proposed as a plain `instrument: String` field carrying
`draft.inst_id` — projectable, but rejected: the only place a pair
label renders on the create screen uses `"${baseCcy}/${quoteCcy}"`, a
different, slash-separated shape, so binding to a raw dash-separated
`inst_id` would have been a silent format mismatch (and worse, legacy
resolves a server-driven display-currency alias via `getDisplayId()`
before the slash swap, which raw `inst_id` can't represent at all).
Readmitted once the correct, already-exported, byte-identical
formatter was found: `core_trading::utils::trade_title_utils::
format_trade_title(inst_id, inst_type)` — an explicit Rust port of
legacy `TradeTitleUtils.getTitleByIdAndType`, already consumed by
TWAP's create/detail flows.

Named `pair_label`, not `pair_title` — this crate already has TWO
other same-shaped fields fed by a sibling formatter, and conflating
any of the three risks reaching for the wrong one:
- **`pair_label`** (this field, create screen) —
`format_trade_title` → `format_spot_title`: `display_id ?: inst_id`,
then `-` → `/`, **no case change**. Matches legacy
`TradeTitleUtils.formatSpotTitle`, the oracle for
`BotTradeHeader.refreshCoinPairsNormal`.
- **`edit_params::pair_title`** (`SpotGridEditParamsState`, from
`info.coin_title_display`) — a different field on a different
surface, sourced from `core::utils::format_util::coin_title_display`.
- **`detail.rs::resolve_biz_display_id` +
`core::utils::format_util::coin_title_display`** — Detail / Orders
/ History. Do not conflate with this field.

All three now agree on **no case folding** — `coin_title_display`
previously `.to_uppercase()`d unconditionally, a bug fixed 2026-09-04
(it mirrored legacy's MARGIN/CONVERT branch, which SPOT never
reaches; see `core/utils/format_util.rs::coin_title_display`'s doc
comment). They remain three separate formatters for three surfaces —
not duplication to consolidate — because each is keyed to its own
legacy call path and could still be corrected independently in the
future; don't merge them.

fields.name: leverage

Leverage badge shown next to the pair label for a SPOT/MARGIN
instrument currently trading on margin (e.g. `"5x"`) — legacy
`BotTradeHeader.refreshCoinPairsNormal`'s `SpotInstrument` + non-blank
`level` badge, gated to Smart Iceberg / TWAP.

`None`, not an empty-string `BotDisplayText`, for every bot/route that
has no such badge (contract-leverage bots, plain-SPOT routes with no
margin leverage resolved) — a prior design note on this exact field
established absence, not a blank value, as the "no badge" contract, so
a spot bot is never forced to carry a spurious empty leverage string.
Added last (uniffi records serialize positionally): appending here
keeps every existing native decode of this record byte-compatible.

See `TwapPlaceOrderJourneyInteractor::create_chrome` for the
reference source (`state.is_spot_margin` + `effective_leverage`).

Additive-only, uniffi-exported record. **A field belongs here only when
an interactor can project it from state it already computes AND a
consumer can use it in the shape provided.** Projectability alone is not
a strong enough test: a create screen's toolbar title is a static
per-bot native string resource (not Rust-supplied data, so no source);
Spot Grid's inline-kline visibility is local view state toggled by a
user tap that Rust does not track (no source). When a bot needs a
chrome field that doesn't exist yet, that bot's slice adds it with a
real source AND a real, shape-checked consumer. See
`SpotGridPlaceOrderInteractor::create_chrome` for the reference
implementation.

name: signal_bot_order_extras_android
doc:
Android twin of the side/reduce-only half of the open-order card.

Native oracle: `getTradeText(instType, side, posSide)`
(OKTradeCore `StrategyConvert.kt:1211-1242`), whose `Pair<String, Boolean>`
second element feeds `getSideColor` / `getSideBgColor` (`:1663-1677`) and thus
the four `tradeRiseTagContent` / `tradeFallTagContent` / `tradeRiseTagFill` /
`tradeFallTagFill` theme attrs. Rust decides the direction; native keeps the
attr->ARGB mapping, whose resolved values are not provable in this workspace.

Two comparison rules that are NOT uniform, and are silent if swapped:
* `inst_type` — native uses `when (instType)`, i.e. structural equality, so
it is **case-SENSITIVE**. `"swap"` falls to the `else` arm.
* `side` / `pos_side` — native uses `equals(x, true)`, so both are
**case-INSENSITIVE**. Mirrored with `eq_ignore_ascii_case`, which is
ASCII-only where Java folds full Unicode. The gap is unreachable from the
OKX wire format (these fields are ASCII enums) but it is a narrowing, not
an exact equivalence, so do not restate it as one.

The `pos_side` arm order also matters: long, then short, then a catch-all that
covers blank and any other value (reachable on one-way-mode rows).

There is no failure path: this is a pure function of three wire strings with
no instrument load, so it cannot raise `instrument_not_found` and returns a
plain `Vec` rather than an `Option`.

name: load

Reproduces the **ANDROID** contract bug-for-bug:
`HistoryPositionFragment.onVisible()` re-fires
`requestHistoryPositions()` with the presenter's RETAINED page —

`viewWillAppear:` either refreshes page 1 (`data.count == 0` +
`autoRefreshOnEmpty`) or leaves the list alone apart from an
expiry-driven `beginRefreshing`, which is also page 1 — it never
re-requests the retained page. The Swift tab accordingly uses only
`refresh` / `load_more`. Kept unchanged because Android is the caller;
an earlier revision of this doc called the Android fragment "Native",
which is the same wrong-baseline wording that produced the unbounded
`has_more` and the load-more page skip.

name: bot_contract_lot_size_validation
doc:
Bridge native's contract lot-size validation
(`ContractTradeInputUtils.getAmtTickSizeMsg`, `TradeInputUtils.kt:529-565`).
`amount` is the value in the user's ALREADY-RESOLVED display unit — the same
value `ContractDcaClosePositionBottomSheet` feeds into `TradeInputUtils
.getAmtTickSizeMsg` today — matching what native validates.

Branch selection mirrors native exactly:
* `TradeUnit::U` (any contract type) -> no check, native's own no-op.
* linear (`!is_inverse`) + Coin/Contract -> `lot_sz` converted into the
display unit via the SAME `OriginQuantityToUserSettingUnitConvertor` that
already backs [`resolve_size_unit`] / [`convert_size_to_user_unit`] (no
price needed — native itself passes a dummy `price = "1"` for this
branch, confirming it is price-independent for linear contracts).
* inverse (`is_inverse`) + Contract -> raw `lot_sz`, no conversion (matches
native using `bizInstrument.getLotSize()` directly for this branch).
* inverse + Coin -> no check, native's own no-op.
* `TradeUnit::Lot` -> `None` (cannot determine): native additionally gates
Lot on a TradFi "Rust CEX" flag (`isTradeUseRustV1()`) that swaps the
board-lot step for a `10^-lotDig` TradFi convention this crate has no read
for. Guessing which rule applies risks a wrong lot size, so this returns
`None` rather than silently picking one.
* `TradeUnit::Unknown` -> `None`: native's real trade-unit setting never
produces this value — it is this crate's own fail-closed default
(`map_trade_unit`) when the convertor cannot classify a unit.

`None` also for: gate off / blank instId or amount / unparseable amount /
unresolvable instrument / unresolvable unit conversion. Native's own
"safe-parse-to-zero" behavior for a malformed amount is deliberately NOT
reproduced (`docs/conventions/money_math.md` bans silent-zero parsing) —
callers get "cannot determine", not a fabricated pass or fail.

The digit follows native `getCoinPrecision`, which branches on whether this
leg IS the invest ccy: the quote leg uses

leg uses the instrument's `baseDig`. `"USDT-USDT"` is not an instrument, so

as a real constituent.

fields.doc:
`marketValue / mktCap` as a percent — UP for a USDT leg, DOWN otherwise,
both `toMax: 2` so trailing zeros are **TRIMMED** (`min_digit` stays 0).

ONE twin serves two rows: Overview's `getCurrentAllocation` and
Parameters' `getCurrentRatioText` compute this identically. A test asserts
that equality so a change to one call site cannot silently drift.

fields.name: current_ratio
fields.doc:
The SAME quantity as [`Self::current_ratio_display`], but RAW: the
unscaled `marketValue / marketCap` fraction (e.g. "0.35" for 35%), with no
percent formatting and no display rounding — only the wire-format bound
`SP_RATIO_RAW_DP` imposes (20 dp, half-up, because the donut parses this
with `NSDecimalNumber` and its silent failure mode is zero).

Both exist because the two consumers need different things from one
computation: the Overview / Parameters ROWS need the rendered percent
(per-coin rounding: USDT up, everything else down), while the allocation
DONUT needs a number for slice geometry. Reading a rendered percent back
into a number would re-parse a value that was deliberately rounded for
display, and computing the fraction again in Swift would put money math
back on the native side.

EMPTY means "omit this slice", not zero: it carries the donut's two numeric
inclusion rules, so the leg is dropped unless `cur_num * px` AND the
resulting fraction are both strictly positive — which is how native's
per-leg `marketValue > 0` guard and its whole-list `mktCap > 0` guard are
expressed on a per-leg field. Also empty when either operand is absent or
unparseable — never a bogus "0".

fields.name: indicator

fields.name: trigger_cond
fields.doc:
Raw trigger-condition wire literal: `"cross_up"`, `"cross_down"`,
`"above"`, `"below"`, `"cross"`, or `""` when absent.

Populated for `Rsi` (drives `formatTriggerCond` in the RSI alert) and
for `Price` (drives the `formatTriggerStrategy` price branch — cross_up
→ "Price crosses above", cross_down → "Price crosses below", anything
else → "Price trigger"). Swift maps the literal to localized copy;
an unrecognised literal renders `--` there, matching native
`formatTriggerCondWithType:`'s `kOKTPOEmptyPlaceholder` fall-through.

fields.name: trigger_px
fields.doc:
Raw trigger price (`Price` only), `""` when absent.

Native renders it through the instrument's charge convertor at both
call sites, so no precision or formatting decision is made here.

fields.name: thold
fields.doc:
RSI threshold (`Rsi` only), already resolved by native's
`getTholdValue` rule: prefer `oversoldThold`, fall back to `thold`
(`OKTSOrderSignParamsModel.m:213-218`).

The two keys exist because the server is deprecating `oversoldThold`
in favour of `thold` while the order API still writes the old key
(`.h:87`) — picking the wrong one shows a stale threshold, so the
choice is made once in Rust. `""` when neither key is present.

fields.name: time_period
fields.doc:
RSI indicator period (`Rsi` only). Defaults to `"14"` when the server
omits the key, mirroring native's `startModel.timePeriod ?: @"14"`
(`OKTSmartIcebergInfoVC.m:178`). An explicitly-empty server value is
preserved as `""` — native's `?:` fires on nil only.

fields.name: timeframe
fields.doc:
Raw K-line timeframe wire literal (`Rsi` only): `"3m"`, `"1H"`, `"1D"`,
… Swift renders it via the localized
`OKTRSITriggerItem.getKLineTimeFrameTitleWithValue:` template.
`""` when absent.

fields.name: delay_seconds
fields.doc:
Delayed-start seconds (`Rsi` alert only), `""` when absent. Swift
formats the number and pairs it with the "Delayed Start" label — see
the `isStartTriggerAction` row of the table above for why the label is
never "Delayed Stop" on this screen.

doc:
Smart Iceberg start-trigger condition — the durable subset of native
`OKTSOrderSignParamsModel` that the Smart Iceberg detail screen reads.

Reached natively as `OKTStgyInfoModel.startTriggerModel`. The native type
carries ~30 members serving grid / DCA / signal bots; only the three
Smart Iceberg consumers below are modelled here:

1. Start Condition **row value** — `OKTSmartIceOperationConfig.m:163-173`.
2. **RSI detail alert** — `OKTSmartIcebergInfoVC.m:177-188`.
3. **Price detail alert** — `OKTSmartIcebergInfoVC.m:190-198`.

# Rust owns the values and the decisions; Swift owns every string

Every native helper these three call was classified before porting:

| Native helper | Verdict | Where it lives now |
|---|---|---|
| `isIndicatorInstance` / `isIndicatorPrice` / `isIndicatorRSI` | **Business logic** — a two-field precedence ladder, not formatting | Rust: resolved into [`indicator`](Self::indicator) |
| `getTholdValue` | **Business logic** — picks `oversoldThold` over `thold`; the server is mid-migration between the two keys | Rust: resolved into [`thold`](Self::thold) |
| `timePeriod ?: @"14"` (`OKTSmartIcebergInfoVC.m:178`) | **Business default** — RSI's default indicator period, not a display string | Rust: resolved into [`time_period`](Self::time_period) |
| `isStartTriggerAction` (`.m:185`) | **Constant-true here** — this Record is only ever built from the entry whose `triggerAction` IS `"start"`, so native's ternary can never take the "Delayed Stop" branch | Dropped; Swift renders "Delayed Start" unconditionally |
| `formatTriggerCond` | **Pure formatting** — a 5-way `OKLocalString` lookup over the `triggerCond` literal (`OKTSOrderSignParamsModel.m:309-331`) | Swift, from [`trigger_cond`](Self::trigger_cond) |
| `formatTriggerStrategy` | **Pure formatting at this call site** — `actionQuestionBtnPrice` only runs when `isIndicatorPrice`, so the method's price branch (`.m:376-383`) is the only reachable one: cross_up / cross_down / else, each an `OKLocalString` | Swift, from [`indicator`](Self::indicator) + [`trigger_cond`](Self::trigger_cond) |
| `OKTRSITriggerItem.getKLineTimeFrameTitleWithValue:` | **Pure formatting** — splits `"3m"`/`"1H"`/`"1D"` into a localized template | Swift, from [`timeframe`](Self::timeframe) |
| `chargeConvertor toQuoteFormated:` (price row + price alert) | **Pure formatting** — instrument-precision + locale grouping | Swift, from [`trigger_px`](Self::trigger_px) |

Numeric scalars stay `String` (precision-preserving) exactly as the native
side already exposes them: it parses each into `NSDecimalNumber` and hands
`toPlainString` — a non-localized, non-grouped rendering — to the display
layer, so passing the wire text through is equivalent. No arithmetic is
performed on any of these values in Rust.

name: SpotDcaDetailEvent
doc:
One-off UI events emitted by the interactor.

All terminal arms surface through durable state fields (`tab_state:
GridTabState`, `is_loading: bool`, `error: Option<String>`, plus the
derived flags `can_pause` / `can_resume` etc. driven by `bot_info`).
The screen does not currently emit transient toasts — Rust no
longer ships English UX copy; native composes localized text from
the durable state fields per `naming.md:139`. Per `interactor.md`
§ "Terminal results surface via durable state, not events", we use the `_PlaceholderEvent`
escape hatch rather than declaring a `ShowToast` variant we never
emit.

name: ArbLegLeverOutcome

variants.name: NoRow
variants.doc:
No matching row — native's `marginInfoByPosSide:` returned nil, or the side
was neither buy nor sell. Native's value is `nil`.

variants.name: NotApplicable
variants.doc:
A row exists but reports its OWN margin mode and that mode disagrees with the
leg's, so the leverage does not apply. Native substitutes
`kOKTPOEmptyPlaceholder` (`hotFixLever:`, `OKTASPOButtonLineVC.m:454-462`).

variants.name: Value
variants.doc: The leverage to display, verbatim.

doc:
What the lever control should show for one position side.

Three outcomes, kept distinct instead of collapsing into `Option<String>`,
because native has three and two of them are NOT the same thing:
"no row at all" and "a row whose leverage does not apply" render the same
placeholder today but arise from different states, and an empty-string sentinel
is exactly the collapse that produced this screen's earlier defects.

Rust does not emit the placeholder TEXT — `naming.md` forbids user-facing
localized strings here, and `kOKTPOEmptyPlaceholder` / `kOKTPONoLoginLeverValue`
are host constants. The host maps [`Self::NoRow`] / [`Self::NotApplicable`] onto
whichever of its own placeholders native uses at that call site.

name: ensure_bot_trade_data_loaded
doc:
Host-triggered warm-up of the shared core-trading trade data (SPOT biz +
coins). Called by the Android bot trade page on entry so deeplink cold
starts don't hit an empty instrument store. Gated by the core-trading gate
(`core_trading_gate::use_core_trading_rust`); idempotent single-flight,
never fails (load errors are logged and swallowed downstream). A cancelled
warm-up is simply dropped — the underlying loaders are idempotent
single-flight, so the next call resumes/reuses the load.
